campaign_note: Sansec names this flaw PolyShell (unauthenticated file upload via the Magento REST API); probing began 2026-03-16, mass exploitation 2026-03-19, with Magecart-style loader injection on hundreds of stores; Adobe backported the fix in APSB26-73 on 2026-07-14.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Sansec (PolyShell research page timeline: "First PolyShell attacks observed in the wild"; probing noted from 2026-03-16)

evidence.counts_what: Magento stores detected compromised (loader injected) in a single hour via PolyShell
evidence.quote: Sansec detected 471 stores compromised in a single hour as attackers exploit the PolyShell vulnerability at scale.

evidence.counts_what: Same 471-store figure restated in trade press with the explicit PolyShell = CVE-2026-48356 mapping (article is about a 953-store loader campaign active since July 2025, of which only the 471 are attributed to this CVE)
evidence.measured_by: Sansec, as reported by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: 471 Magento stores are estimated to have been injected with the loader through the PolyShell

evidence.counts_what: Share of Sansec-monitored stores hit with malicious upload attempts (attack attempts against protected stores, not confirmed compromises)
evidence.quote: 82% of all stores hit with malicious uploads

evidence.counts_what: Share of Sansec Shield-protected Magento stores against which PolyShell exploitation attempts were blocked since 2026-03-16
evidence.quote: has blocked PolyShell exploitation attempts against 79.5% of all protected Magento stores since March 16th.
Since March 23, Sansec has recorded more than 50 IPs probing for PolyShell attacks.

campaign_note: Sekoia's 'Poisoned Source' report (2026-11-04) describes APT29-attributed watering holes, including a compromise of the Plerdy analytics tracker, serving an iOS 16.7 n-day chain that uses CVE-2024-27834 as a PAC bypass for cookie theft; no device or victim count was published.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Sekoia ('Poisoned Source' report; activity discovered mid-October 2026, Plerdy compromise window 2026-08-27 to 2026-09-03)

evidence.counts_what: Legitimate websites (and their visitors) exposed to the exploit kit through the compromised Plerdy tracker for one week; this is delivery reach, not devices compromised, and covers the whole kit rather than this CVE alone
evidence.quote: exposing hundreds of legitimate websites and their visitors to its exploit kit for one week.

evidence.counts_what: Lookalike reverse-proxy websites set up by the actor to deliver the exploit kit
evidence.quote: We identified two high-profile websites set up by the intrusion set to act as reverse proxies.

campaign_note: Arista detected active exploitation itself and disclosed it with the patch on 2026-10-22; it is the third exploited VCO flaw since July 2026 (after CVE-2026-16812 and CVE-2026-93952), and Arista says hosted/dedicated VCO instances were impacted, with no victim or exposure count published.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Arista Security Advisory 0199 ("This issue was detected by Arista and is known to be actively exploited.")

evidence.counts_what: Attacker IP addresses listed by the vendor as observed conducting the attacks (74.82.197.86, 38.54.50.151)
evidence.quote: The following IP addresses have been observed conducting the attacks.

evidence.value: hosted and dedicated VCO impacted (no count)
evidence.counts_what: Vendor statement that its hosted/dedicated orchestrators were impacted; unquantified
evidence.quote: Hosted, including Dedicated, versions of VCO were impacted and have already been patched.

campaign_note: Patched 2026-11-02 together with CVE-2026-116606 (chainable on ESG for pre-auth root); Barracuda updated its advisory on 2026-11-09 to report exploitation affecting 'a small number of organizations', with no count and no trade-press quantification found.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Barracuda advisory update (9:00pm EST): exploitation information added

evidence.counts_what: Organizations affected by observed exploitation activity (unquantified; advisory covers both chained CVEs)
evidence.quote: We have identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations.

campaign_note: ESG authentication bypass chained with CVE-2026-111560 for root; patched 2026-11-02, exploitation affecting 'a small number of organizations' acknowledged by Barracuda on 2026-11-09, no count published.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Barracuda advisory update (9:00pm EST): exploitation information added

evidence.counts_what: Organizations affected by observed exploitation activity (unquantified; advisory covers both chained CVEs)
evidence.quote: We added information about exploitation activity that has been observed affecting a small number of organizations.

campaign_note: Zero-day exploited since late August 2026 by a suspected China-nexus espionage actor (Mandiant 'Armory Castle' / CrowdStrike 'Warp Panda') deploying the Sawfly web shell and Bareclaw tunneler; BeyondTrust reports two known compromises (one hosted instance, one self-hosted appliance) and patched SaaS on 2026-10-08 before disclosing on 2026-10-15.

first_exploitation_claim.source: BeyondTrust advisory BT26-05 (vendor page returned HTTP 403; date and claim taken from BleepingComputer and Rapid7 coverage)

evidence.counts_what: Known Remote Support compromises: one BeyondTrust-hosted instance and one self-hosted appliance, both dated to 2026-08-29
evidence.measured_by: BeyondTrust (16 Oct 2026 report), as relayed by Rapid7
evidence.quote: dates the two known Remote Support compromises to August 29, 2026

evidence.counts_what: BeyondTrust Remote Support instances exposed online (patch status unknown; may include honeypots)
evidence.quote: tracks over 1,400 BeyondTrust remote support instances exposed online

evidence.counts_what: Operational impact described by Mandiant: root on the appliance and access to stored/brokered credentials; no downtime or data-theft volume reported
evidence.quote: access to every credential the appliance stored or brokered

campaign_note: CrowdStrike's 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report (2026-10-28) says China-nexus Warp Panda used this low-severity (CVSS 2.7) logging flaw as a zero-day in several intrusions at US organizations including law firms, continuing into early 2026; no victim count for this CVE was found.

first_exploitation_claim.source: CrowdStrike 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report, as reported by SecurityWeek (SecurityWeek page returned HTTP 403; claim read from search summary and a secondary write-up, primary report not retrieved)

evidence.counts_what: Intrusions in which Warp Panda used the flaw (unquantified); quote is from a lower-tier trade outlet relaying CrowdStrike because SecurityWeek blocked fetching
evidence.measured_by: CrowdStrike, as relayed by Cyber Security News
evidence.quote: CrowdStrike identified the group as WARP PANDA and said it used the flaw

campaign_note: Unauthenticated XXE in the BroadWorks OCI XML parser, patched 2026-08-19; coverage found reflects only the advisory-date status, when Cisco reported no known exploitation, and no report describing the exploitation behind the KEV listing was found.
